epic.intent:
Make the desktop app look like it belongs to the Adeptus Mechanicus, matching the app icon.

**Today:** the renderer uses a generic graphite "forge console" palette with an amber accent (`src/renderer/src/styles.css`), and the sidebar brand is a stroke hex glyph. The chibi tech-priest appears in the dock/taskbar and the favicon, but nowhere a person actually looks inside the app.

**Outcome:** a palette taken from the icon (Mars crimson hood and robe, bone/ivory cog trim, brass fittings, gunmetal respirator, with the green cybernetic lens as a sparing highlight) applied across the shell, sidebar, home, epic workspace, plan graph, ticket panel and checkpoint screens. The tech-priest becomes the sidebar brand mark and greets people on the welcome and onboarding screens.

**Why:** the app should feel like one product with its icon, and the palette change is a chance to route every color through tokens and guard contrast with a test.

**Out of scope:** layout or information-architecture changes, new features, a light theme, new fonts, regenerating the icon artwork, and packaging icons (`build/icon.icns`, `build/icon.ico`; done in board epic 019).

successCriteria.text: The desktop app's colors come from a Mechanicus palette derived from the app icon (crimson, bone, brass, gunmetal), documented in `docs/design/palette.md`.
Every renderer color flows through `:root` tokens in `src/renderer/src/styles.css`; no component stylesheet hardcodes a hex color.
The sidebar brand shows the tech-priest icon, and the welcome and onboarding screens show the mascot.
Every ticket and run state stays distinguishable from the brand colors and from each other, and always shows its text label.
Body text and state labels meet WCAG AA contrast (at least 4.5:1) on their surfaces, enforced by a unit test.
Lint, typecheck, unit tests, fireguard, deadcode and build pass on the integrated branch.

epic.title: Mechanicus UI revamp: crimson, brass and the tech-priest mascot

bundle.rationale:
**Shape.** Two sprints. Sprint 1 does the safe groundwork in parallel (token consolidation, the palette proposal, the sidebar brand mark), so the sprint 1 checkpoint is a real decision: the person approves the palette before anyone applies it. Sprint 2 applies the palette (with a contrast guard test written first), then restyles the shell and the epic workspace in parallel, adds the mascot to the first-run screens, and ends with an integration ticket.

**Critical path:** palette (or token consolidation) → apply palette → shell or workspace restyle → integrate.

**Integration ticket.** The shell restyle and the mascot ticket both edit `src/renderer/src/styles.css`, and the workspace restyle edits the shared tones, so the integration ticket owns merging, conflict resolution, the full check suite, the design README, and evidence for each success criterion.

**Assumptions** (from a one-line request; change any of these before saving):
- The app stays dark-only, with IBM Plex type and the current layout. This is a color and branding pass, not a redesign.
- Crimson is the primary accent, brass the secondary, bone for display text. The lens green appears sparingly.
- The icon artwork is final. Packaging icons are already done (board epic 019), so this epic only uses the icon inside the renderer.
- The static mockups in `docs/design/mockups/` are not regenerated. The README notes that they predate the revamp.
- Visual changes are verified with screenshots attached to submissions, and contrast is enforced by a unit test.

exitCriteria.text: Every renderer color flows through `:root` tokens in `styles.css`, with no visual change.
`docs/design/palette.md` proposes the full token set with roles, collision rules and a contrast table, ready for the person to approve at this checkpoint.
The sidebar brand shows the tech-priest icon, and the favicon matches the current icon.

acceptanceCriteria.text: No hex color literal appears in renderer CSS outside the `:root` token block of `src/renderer/src/styles.css`.

tickets.body:
Later in this epic the palette swap should only change values in the `:root` block of `src/renderer/src/styles.css`. Right now a few component stylesheets hardcode their own colors:

- `graph/graph.css`: `#8a8070` (`--xy-edge-stroke`, the accepted edge stroke, the sprint divider), `#6a6254` (waiting edge, waiting divider), `#1d1a16` (node background)
- `epic/tones.css`: `#e8b86a` (`.ew-tone-edited`)
- `styles.css`: `#f0c27a` (`a:hover`)

Give each one a token in `:root` named for what it colors (for example `--edge`, `--edge-waiting`, `--node-bg`, `--tone-edited`, `--accent-hover`) and use that token instead. Every rendered color must stay exactly the same. This ticket is a refactor with no visual change.

**In scope:** renderer CSS only.
**Out of scope:** changing any color value. Literal `rgba(0, 0, 0, …)` box-shadows can stay.

**Verify:** `grep -rnE '#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b' src/renderer/src --include='*.css'` only matches lines inside the `:root` block of `styles.css`.

reasoning.rationale: Mechanical token extraction with no behavior change.

tickets.title: Move hardcoded renderer colors into theme tokens

acceptanceCriteria.text: `docs/design/palette.md` lists every `:root` color token with its current value, proposed value and role.
The doc names the primary accent, the secondary accent, and where the lens green may appear.
The doc explains how the crimson accent stays distinct from failed/danger and the green from accepted, including any re-tuned state values.
The contrast table shows at least 4.5:1 for every text and state-label pair listed in the ticket, and at least 3:1 for `--faint`.
Each proposed brand value can be traced to a color sampled from `build/icon.png`.

tickets.body:
Decide the new color tokens before anyone touches the theme. Take the palette from the chibi tech-priest in `build/icon.png` (the master is `build/mechanicus-cute-master.png`): Mars crimson hood and robe, bone/ivory cog trim, brass fittings, gunmetal respirator, and the green cybernetic lens.

Write `docs/design/palette.md` with:

1. **Token table.** Every color token in `:root` of `src/renderer/src/styles.css` (surfaces, lines, text, accent, states, danger, and the tokens added by the token-consolidation ticket), each with its current value, proposed value and role.
2. **Roles.** The primary accent (primary buttons, focus ring, selection, active sidebar row), the secondary accent (rules, highlights, links), display/heading ink, and where the green lens glow is allowed. Use it sparingly, for example the brand glow or the running indicator.
3. **Collision rules.** The crimson accent must not read as `--st-failed` or `--danger`, and the lens green must not read as `--st-accepted`. Re-tune state colors where needed and say how each state stays distinct (hue distance plus its text label).
4. **Contrast table** (WCAG 2.x ratios) for `--ink`, `--ink-2` and `--muted` on `--bg`, `--panel`, `--panel-2` and `--sidebar`; every `--st-*` on `--panel`; `--accent-ink` on `--accent`; `--danger-ink` on `--danger`. Body text and state labels need at least 4.5:1. `--faint` (decorative only) needs at least 3:1.

Starting samples from the icon (approximate, so check them against the image): crimson about `#b3201c` to `#c62a22`, deep hood shadow about `#480101`, bone trim about `#deba94` to `#e9dcc0`, brass about `#b5893a`, gunmetal about `#2a2624`, lens green about `#84c20a`.

Keep the dark-only theme, the IBM Plex fonts and the current layout. **Out of scope:** editing any stylesheet. The "Apply the Mechanicus palette" ticket does that once the person approves this doc at the sprint 1 checkpoint.

reasoning.rationale: Balancing brand hues against distinct state colors and contrast takes deliberate trade-offs.

tickets.body: The sidebar brand (`Brand` in `src/renderer/src/sidebar/Sidebar.tsx`) shows a stroke hex glyph (``). Replace it with the app icon so the window carries the same mascot as the dock and taskbar. - Generate small renderer assets from `build/icon.png`, for example 32 px and 64 px for a 1x/2x display size of about 28 to 32 px. Put them under `src/renderer/src/assets/` and import them through Vite so they are hashed and bundled. Keep each file small (aim for under 20 KB). - Render an `` with a 1x/2x `srcSet`. It sits next to the `DARK MECHANICUS` text, so it is decorative: `alt=""`. - The CSP already allows `img-src 'self' data: file:` (`electron.vite.config.ts`). Do not loosen it. - Regenerate `src/renderer/public/favicon.png` (64 px) from the current `build/icon.png` so it matches the approved revision. - If nothing else uses the `hex` icon path in `components/Icon.tsx`, remove it so `npm run deadcode` stays clean. - Write the Sidebar test change first: the brand renders the image and still shows the name and version. **Out of scope:** packaging icons (`build/icon.icns`, `build/icon.ico`), regenerating artwork, palette changes.

reasoning.rationale: A small component change with an asset pipeline step and a test.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every `:root` color token in `src/renderer/src/styles.css` matches its value in `docs/design/palette.md`.
A contrast guard test reads the tokens from `styles.css` and enforces the pairs and thresholds from the palette doc. Changing a token so that it breaks contrast makes the test fail.
The guard test was written before the token change and fireguard grades it above F.
Screenshots of the welcome screen, a folder home and a plan graph in the new palette are attached to the submission.
`npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run fireguard`, `npm run deadcode` and `npm run build` pass.

tickets.body:
Change the `:root` token values in `src/renderer/src/styles.css` to the palette in `docs/design/palette.md`, which the person approved at the sprint 1 checkpoint. Because the token-consolidation ticket routed every color through `:root`, this should only change values in that one block.

**TDD first:** add a Vitest test (for example `src/renderer/src/theme.contrast.test.ts`) that parses the `:root` block of `styles.css`, computes WCAG contrast ratios, and asserts the pairs and thresholds from the contrast table in the palette doc. Write it against the new values, watch it fail on the old ones, then change the tokens.

Also update the header comment in `styles.css` that describes the theme. Component-level polish belongs to the two restyle tickets that follow. Keep this ticket to token values plus the guard test.

**Verify:** run `npm run dev` and screenshot the welcome screen, a folder home and an epic plan graph.

reasoning.rationale: Introduces a contrast guard test and swaps the whole token set, which every screen depends on.

tickets.body:
With the new token values in place, adjust the component rules in `src/renderer/src/styles.css` that look wrong in crimson, brass and bone: the sidebar (active and hover rows, bucket headers, footer), the brand bar, buttons (primary, ghost, danger), pills, cards, dialogs, menus, toasts, the update banner, onboarding, and the folder home (MCP card, storage card, branch epics, history search).

**Direction:** crimson for primary actions and the active selection, brass for rules and secondary highlights, bone for display text on dark surfaces, all following the roles in `docs/design/palette.md`. Small Mechanicus touches are welcome if they stay subtle and token-based, for example a brass hairline under the brand bar or a cog-tooth divider. Add no new layout and no new fonts, and use no inline styles (the CSP is `style-src 'self'`).

**Out of scope:** the epic workspace, graph, ticket panel and checkpoint stylesheets (they have their own ticket); the mascot illustration on the welcome and onboarding screens (also its own ticket).

**Verify:** before and after screenshots of the welcome screen (no folders), onboarding, a folder home, the sidebar with a folder expanded, a dialog and a toast.

reasoning.rationale: Visual tuning across many shell components that must stay consistent with the palette roles.

tickets.body:
Put the tech-priest on the first-run screens. Reuse the renderer icon assets added for the sidebar brand mark, and add a larger size (for example 128 px and 256 px) if needed.

- `components/EmptyState.tsx`: add an optional illustration slot (for example `illustration?: ReactNode`) that renders above the title instead of the stroke icon. Write the EmptyState test first.

lint, typecheck, tests, fireguard, deadcode and build all pass on the integrated branch.

tickets.body:
The shell restyle, the workspace restyle and the mascot ticket all touch renderer files, especially `src/renderer/src/styles.css` and the onboarding and empty-state rules. Bring them together on the epic branch and verify the whole revamp.

1. Merge the commits from those tickets onto the epic feature branch and resolve conflicts, especially in `styles.css`.
2. Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run fireguard`, `npm run deadcode` and `npm run build`.
3. Run the app (`npm run dev`) and take one screenshot each of: the welcome screen, onboarding, a folder home, a plan graph mid-run, the ticket panel, a sprint checkpoint, a dialog, and the update banner if you can reach it.
4. Update the "Visual direction" section of `docs/design/README.md` to describe the Mechanicus palette, link `docs/design/palette.md`, and note that the static mockups predate the revamp.
5. Check each epic success criterion and report evidence for it.

**Out of scope:** new styling beyond conflict resolution and small fixes found during verification.

reasoning.rationale: Merges parallel UI branches touching the same stylesheet and verifies every success criterion.
